newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-May 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-May 9.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- Some members of China's Preparatory Committee, charged with overseeing Hong Kong's handover to Chinese rule on July 1, criticised the post-handover provisional legislature for not doing its job properly and failing to give priority to important and urgent issues.
-- SING TAO DAILY -- At least 32 people died when a China Southern Airlines Boeing 737 crash-landed in Shenzhen during a thunderstorm.
-- Chen Ziying, deputy director of China's Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office, hinted that the Preparatory Committee had completed its mission and could be disbanded.
-- WEN WEI PO -- During a meeting with U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan, Chinese President Jiang Zemin said Hong Kong would continue to be a bridge which linked China with the outside world.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- The Hong Kong Stock Exchange had completed a new set of regulations on listed companies spinning off parts of their businesses. The new rules, to be announced shortly, say listed companies cannot spin off the businesses which make up the best parts of their turnover and profit.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Share prices on mainland exchanges posted their sharpest single-day decline since February 18, triggered by rumours Beijing would act to remove speculative froth from the markets.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- A China expert said the mainland is facing a severe unemployment problem, but those who advocate closing the cities to rural labourers have ignored the principle of fair competition.
-- Accountants said Hong Kong banks had to tighten internal control standards to deal with rising credit risks brought about by competition and increased lending to China.
